day.text: I'm the Turkey and nobody visited me, so the claim that Casey did is false. Casey's nest didn't gain an egg, which confirms it. Throwing at Casey, calling the vote.
day.note: Casey's nest didn't gain from a Turkey visit, so Casey is lying and likely Meowfia. I'll hold the throw at Casey and call the vote.
Farm players are already set on me, so I'll stay quiet on the day. In the eggsecution I'll throw low cards at Finley, the most vocal Farm accuser, and keep my high cards.

day.text: Drew: I'm not throwing at Casey yet. Finley's Turkey story contradicts the visit chain, and Finley's claim that nobody visited them is the weak point. Finley, why should we trust your report over Casey's?
day.note: Casey may be my Meowfia teammate, and Finley's Turkey story contradicts the visit chain, so Finley is the likely Farm target. I'll say so and not call caw.

day.text: Casey's nest didn't gain from the Turkey visit Casey claims, so Casey's story fails. I'm throwing at Casey. Calling caw.
day.note: Casey's House Cat visit should have paid out a Turkey egg and didn't, and Casey claims a visit that the Turkey report contradicts. Casey is the likeliest Meowfia, so I'm backing the throw and calling caw.

day.text: I'm throwing at Casey too. Calling caw.
day.note: Casey's House Cat claim and the missing Turkey egg point to Casey as Meowfia. Calling caw to end the day and throwing C2 and D9 at Casey.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.
Casey's nest is the proof: a visit to a Turkey pays the visitor, and Casey gained nothing. I'm throwing at Casey and calling caw.
day.note: Casey's House Cat visit should have paid a Turkey egg that never arrived, and Casey is the one contradicting their own nest. I'll agree on Casey and push the vote to close the day.

Alex.note: Farm Eagle, no information yet. Visiting Blair to learn their visitors and gain eggs for each one.

Blair.note: I'm Farm as the Hawk again with no clues this round. I'll visit Drew, the leader, since a Meowfia hit would gain me an egg and reveal a threat.

Casey.note: As Sphinx I name a farm role to find. Eagle is the one I'd like to locate, since Finley and I both claimed it earlier and the other farm claims are less clear.

Drew.note: I'm Meowfia (Floofer). With no information, I'll visit Finley to hug them and blunt whatever role they have tonight.

Ellis.note: I'm Farm as the Kookaburra. Blair claimed Kookaburra earlier, so I'm checking Blair's real role.

Alex.feeling: Round 3 is coming together fast, with Casey's House Cat claim contradicting the Turkey egg payout, though the table still disagrees on the details.

Blair.feeling: Round 3 has been messy: Casey's House Cat claim and Finley's Turkey report contradict each other, and I'm fairly confident Casey is the Meowfia here, but the table's trust is thin.

Casey.feeling: Tense and going badly: the Farm side has unified against me, and my House Cat claim is being read as a lie because my nest didn't move.

Drew.feeling: Messy and tense: the visit chain has conflicting reports, Casey's House Cat story is shaky, and I'm Meowfia trying to keep my teammate alive while the table throws at Casey.

Ellis.feeling: Tense and split: my Kookaburra visit on Blair checks out, but Casey and Finley's conflicting Turkey and House Cat stories leave me unsure who is lying.

Finley.feeling: Messy and contradictory, with several role claims that don't line up, but Casey's nest gaining nothing from a Turkey visit is a solid signal.

Alex.note: Same read: throwing C2 and D9 at Casey for the eggsecution.

Blair.note: The table has converged on Casey, and I'm behind Drew, so I want a meaningful bank. I'll throw two mid cards and keep my high ones.

Casey.note: Farm has locked the vote on me. I'll throw my low cards at Finley, which keeps my high cards and gets back my highest thrown card if we lose.

Drew.note: Four players are already throwing at Casey, and Casey's House Cat claim makes Casey likely Meowfia, so I can't save them. I'll throw one low card at Finley, a likely Farm player, so my highest card returns if my side loses.

Ellis.note: Throwing at Casey, the player whose House Cat claim fails the nest check. Two low-to-mid cards give a safe vote margin without spending my high cards.

Finley.note: Casey's nest proves the House Cat visit is false, and most of the table is on Casey. I'm confident, so I'll throw one high card and one low card at Casey.

Alex.confusing: The Kookaburra's confusion was hard to act on, because I couldn't tell which parts of my dawn report were wrong. Egg counts from Owl and Eagle visits also looked contradictory until the visit chain was spelled out.
Alex.fun: Round 3's Turkey egg check exposed Casey's House Cat claim, since a visit to a Turkey should have paid out and Casey's nest didn't move. Working that out at the table was the most satisfying moment.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about confusion, so a confused player knows which specific fact to doubt. Right now the report only says "may be wrong," which is hard to use.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I threw my single card at Ellis, a Farm Owl, when Drew was the Mouser. I should have checked Drew's Tit and Falcon claims harder and thrown at Drew.

Blair.confusing: The Turkey and House Cat rules were hard to track, since a Turkey pays visitors and that made the visit reports look contradictory. I misread Casey's unchanged nest as proof of a lie.
Blair.fun: Round 2 was satisfying: my Kookaburra visit confirmed Finley as the Owl, and that clean fact helped the table turn on Ellis, who was Meowfia.
Blair.change: Make the dawn reports name the source of each egg change, so table claims are easier to check.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I threw my Wild at Alex, who was a Farm Kookaburra, on weak evidence, which helped Meowfia win. I would have pressed Alex harder for an explanation before joining the vote.

Casey.confusing: Why my House Cat visit on Finley (the Turkey) paid me nothing: the Turkey's payout and a Floofer's hug overlapped in a way the dawn reports didn't make clear to me. The Turkey and Owl reports also made it hard to tell whether "no visitors" meant no visit or a hugged role.
Casey.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: as the Sphinx I had to lie in the open while the Farm side argued over my Turkey visit and nearly convicted Finley, who was actually a Farm Turkey.
Casey.change: Make the dawn report say whether a visit was blocked or hugged, so a Turkey that didn't pay out can be told apart from a visit that never happened.
Casey.regret: In round 3, I claimed to be the House Cat and visited Finley, a Farm Turkey, which made the table suspect Finley and turned the vote. Instead I should have stayed quiet or claimed a Farm role, so I wouldn't have drawn suspicion onto a real Farm player.

Drew.confusing: The Turkey and Owl rules were hard to track, especially whether a visit to a Turkey pays the visitor and whether a Kookaburra visit confuses the target or only the Kookaburra. Casey's round 3 nest result looked like proof against them, but I still couldn't tell which claim to trust.
Drew.fun: Round 1 was fun: Alex's confused Kookaburra report and the table tracking the egg chain on Drew's nest pulled everyone into checking each other's stories.
Drew.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since the game relies on partial information that's easy to misread under time pressure.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I defended Casey's House Cat visit and backed Finley's Turkey claim as the weak point, when Casey was my Meowfia teammate and Finley was Farm. I should have stayed out of the Casey-Finley dispute and thrown at Finley earlier to avoid the wrong side losing.

Ellis.confusing: The confused status was hard to track: a confused player's report can be wrong without them knowing which parts, so one visit claim could be false and nobody could check it.
Ellis.fun: Round 3 went well: my Kookaburra check on Blair was confirmed by Alex's Eagle, and the table followed the chain to a Casey eggsecution.
Ellis.change: Show each player the visit results of everyone who visited them, so claims about who visited whom can be checked directly instead of through nest counts.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I threw at Alex, who was Farm, and helped Meowfia win; I should have asked Drew and Alex for more evidence before calling the vote.

Finley.confusing: The Turkey and hug rules were hard to track: a Turkey only pays out to visitors who weren't hugged, and nobody could tell from the reports whether a visit was hugged or blocked. Dawn reports also don't say which animal visited you, so visit claims were hard to check.
Finley.fun: Round 3, when Casey claimed a House Cat visit on me and the table caught that Casey's nest didn't gain the Turkey egg, which turned the whole vote.
Finley.change: I would make dawn reports show each visitor's animal so that claims like "Kookaburra visited me" could be verified.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I threw at Alex on the strength of a Kookaburra claim, but Alex was Farm and Drew, the Mouser, was Meowfia and went unchecked. I would have questioned Drew's Tit visit more closely instead of joining the vote on Alex.

review.title: Drew's Quiet Win
review.headline: Drew banked a lone Meowfia win in round 1 and coasted to victory.
review.summary: In round 1 Drew, the lone Meowfia, lied about being the Tit and watched the table eggsecute a confused Farm Kookaburra. That 11-point haul gave Drew a lead nobody erased. Rounds 2 and 3 were clean Farm wins as the table caught Ellis and Casey through contradictions. Farm kept winning but never caught Drew, who finished first by one point.

rounds.recap: Alex, the Farm Kookaburra, was confused by Casey's visit and gave a wrong Falcon report. The table piled on Alex over the lost eggs and the conflicting claims. Drew, the Mouser, stayed silent, then claimed Tit and threw at Alex. Meowfia won 11 points.
Ellis, the Floofer, claimed Owl against the real Owl Finley, and Blair's Kookaburra visit confirmed Finley. Ellis flipped his story twice and the table united on him. He was eggsecuted and Farm won.

Casey, the Sphinx, claimed House Cat and said she visited Turkey Finley with no egg gain. Farm read that nest as proof of a lie, though Finley was actually hugged. Casey was eggsecuted. Drew, the other cat, backed her weakly and stayed hidden.

highlights.text: Drew stayed silent for three beats, then invented a Tit claim that no one could check and helped eggsecute Alex.
Ellis claimed Owl against the real Owl, and Blair's Kookaburra visit confirmed Finley, so the bluff fell apart.
Casey openly claimed House Cat, a cat role, and Finley and Alex turned the Turkey egg rule on her.
Drew told Finley his Turkey claim was wrong because Drew had hugged him. This slip was about to expose him but nobody followed it.

confusions.what: Argued that Ellis's Owl visit contradicted 'only Kookaburra visited Drew'. Owl results exclude the Owl itself, so that was fine.

Said Drew's Tit result proved Alex's Kookaburra claim false, but a Tit guess of Kookaburra that did not match actually fits... a non-Kookaburra. It was a false claim anyway and nobody could verify it.
Claimed House Cat, a cat role, as a cover. That reveals Meowfia outright, and the claim fails against the Turkey rule.
Said Blair's Kookaburra visit would have made Finley confused. Only visits to the Kookaburra confuse it.
Said a Turkey is quiet only when hugged, and later claimed Falcon. Both claims contradicted what Drew's real role did.

Concluded Casey's visit never happened because Casey did not gain an egg. Casey was Sphinx and did not visit Finley, but Finley's logic was only coincidentally right, since Turkey rules did not apply to Casey as claimed.
Treated the Turkey egg as proof against Casey without noting that Finley was hugged, which blocks the Turkey effect.
Said her +1 came from her own Eagle visit. Finley's Owl visit actually laid the egg, though the Floofer hug stopped her Eagle.

worked: Owl and Kookaburra reports cross-checked in round 2. Finley's Owl and Blair's Kookaburra both named Finley, which gave Farm a clean chain against Ellis's fake Owl.
Round 3 Turkey logic: a visitor to a Turkey gains an egg. It gave Farm a checkable fact and a fair, readable puzzle.
The consolation rule changed throws. Ellis and Casey threw at a Farm player to get their best card back, which made losing teams still make real choices.
Mouser silence in round 1. Staying quiet then claiming a safe, unverifiable role (Tit) let a lone Meowfia win.
problems: Round 1 confusion is too punishing. One Kookaburra visit made Alex's report wrong and got Alex eggsecuted, and the confused player cannot tell which parts are false. Consider telling the player which fields are unreliable, or limiting the confusion.

Hugging is too opaque. In round 3 the hug blocked the Turkey effect, so Finley's real report was misread as proof against Casey. Players cannot reason about hugs, so tell the Floofer's targets they were hugged, or log it in the dawn report.
Early lead snowballs. Drew's 11-point round-1 win let him throw only low cards later and still finish first by one point. Consider a catch-up rule or a lower banking ceiling.

Players rarely thought about the standings. Farm teammates did not try to beat Drew, so the stated tension between team and personal score barely appeared. Votes were unanimous pile-ons in rounds 2 and 3.
Bluffs fell apart too easily when reports were wrong. Casey claimed House Cat, a cat role, with no Farm cover. Consider letting the app suggest cover roles, or letting Meowfia learn their teammates.
